sections.h2: Who records a deed in Lee County, Illinois?
sections.html:
The Lee County Clerk and Recorder records every document that touches real estate in the county, and the same office issues vital records, runs elections and handles delinquent taxes. It sits on the second floor of the Old Lee County Courthouse at 112 E Second Street in Dixon. Hours are 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding legal holidays. The phone is 815-288-3309, and the mailing address is P.O. Box 329, Dixon, IL 61021.

Lee County is a rural county of about 725 square miles in northern Illinois, split from Ogle County in 1839, and Dixon is the county seat. The Census Bureau lists 15,027 housing units there as of July 1, 2025, with 90.5% of residents in the same house a year earlier. That low turnover means most deeds recorded in Lee County cover long-held homes, often with inherited, trust or estate paperwork behind them.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Lee County?
sections.html:
A standard document, which includes a warranty deed, quitclaim deed or mortgage release, costs $88 to record. The fee is $69 when the document is exempt from the Rental Housing Support fee. The county's predictable fee schedule took effect July 1, 2023 and cites 55 ILCS 5/3-5018.1. A state law passed in 2023 raised the Rental Housing Support fee by $9, and that change also took effect July 1, 2023.

The office accepts cash or check only, with no credit or debit cards. A self-addressed stamped envelope is required for each document, and only originals or certified copies are accepted. A copy of a veteran's discharge is recorded at no charge. These fees do not include the transfer tax discussed below, which is a separate charge.

sections.h2: How must a Lee County deed be formatted?
sections.html:
A document that follows the county's format rules pays the standard fee. One that breaks them pays $97. The rules printed on the Recording page are:

  • Loose sheets of 8.5 by 11 inches, not permanently bound and not a continuous form. Graphics up to 11 by 17 inches are allowed at no added charge.
  • Legible black ink, whether handwritten, typed or computer printed. Signatures and dates may use contrasting colors if they copy clearly.
  • White paper of at least 20-pound weight, with a clean half-inch margin on the top, bottom and both sides.
  • A blank space of at least 3 by 5 inches in the upper right corner of the first page.
  • No attachment stapled or otherwise affixed to a page, though the pages themselves may be stapled together.

The recorder's staff will not give legal advice, opinions, legal descriptions or searches, in person or by phone. Get the legal description from your prior deed or the title company, and let an attorney draft anything that changes who owns the house.

sections.h2: Does a Lee County deed need a Plat Act affidavit?
sections.html:
Yes, with one exception named by the county. A plat act affidavit or a plat act exemption must accompany or appear on every deed, except deeds in the Woodhaven Lakes subdivision. The county posts an affidavit form that states the transfer is exempt under the Illinois Plat Act (765 ILCS 205) and lists reasons such as the transfer not dividing land.

Leaving it off is the commonest reason a deed is returned. If you split a parcel to sell part of a lot or a farm field, talk to the assessment office and a surveyor first, since a division of land is where the exemption stops applying.

sections.h2: What transfer tax and declaration apply when a Lee County house sells?
sections.html:
Illinois taxes the transfer of title at 50 cents for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, stated in the declaration (35 ILCS 200/31-10). If the deed says the property passes subject to a mortgage, the unpaid mortgage balance is left out of the calculation. The recorder collects the tax by selling revenue stamps, and paper stamps were scheduled to give way to electronic stamps or similar indicia by December 31, 2025 (35 ILCS 200/31-15).

A transfer declaration must be signed by at least one seller and one buyer, or by their attorneys or agents. It is due when the deed goes in for recording, or within 3 business days after the transfer, whichever is earlier (35 ILCS 200/31-25). The form asks for value, parcel number, legal description, deed type, address, improvements, any homestead exemptions on the last tax bill, and whether the sale was between related parties or compulsory.

Some deeds are exempt from the tax itself, including tax deeds, deeds where the true consideration is under $100, and deeds given to a mortgage holder in foreclosure or in lieu of it (35 ILCS 200/31-45). Several of those still need a declaration. Ask the Clerk and Recorder whether any county or local charge applies in addition to the state tax.

sections.h2: Where does the recorded declaration go next?
sections.html:
The recorder does not record the declaration. The office writes the deed's document number on it and sends it to the chief county assessment officer within 30 days, and that office adds the assessed value and forwards it to the Illinois Department of Revenue (35 ILCS 200/31-30). In practice, that is how the Lee County assessment office learns that a house sold and at what price.

The declaration is the assessment office's record of the sale, so an accurate one protects you as well as the buyer. The same chain of records is why the seller's homestead exemption needs attention after closing. State law leaves the exemption in place for the rest of the assessment year of the sale, and the assessment office may require the new owner to apply for the following year (35 ILCS 200/15-175).

sections.h2: Can a Lee County deed be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes, through approved submitters. The county accepts electronic recordings from 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. and lists four partners:

  • Corporation Service Company (erecording.com)
  • eRecording Partners Network (goepn.com)
  • Simplifile (simplifile.com)
  • Hopdox (hopdox.com)

Title companies and closing attorneys usually file this way on closing day. If you are handling a family transfer without a title company, plan to deliver the paper original by mail with the stamped envelope and a check, or in person during office hours.

sections.h2: What should you check before recording when you sell a house as-is?
sections.html:
Work through the recording steps in order. Confirm the owner of record by searching the parcel on the county's property tax inquiry site, then check for unpaid tax or a tax sale through the Treasurer at 815-288-4477. A buyer's title search will find open mortgages, liens and judgments, and each one has to be released of record or paid at closing.

Inherited homes need extra care. The deed must come from whoever holds title, which can mean a personal representative with court papers, and the recorder will not sort that out for you. Selling a house with repairs, tenants or back taxes does not change the recording mechanics, only who pays the tax and fees at the table.

faqs.q: How much does the Lee County recorder charge for a standard deed?
faqs.a: $88 for a standard document, or $69 when it is exempt from the Rental Housing Support fee, under the fee schedule that took effect July 1, 2023. Non-conforming documents and those citing six or more parcel numbers cost $97.

faqs.q: Can I pay recording fees by card in Lee County?
faqs.a: No. The Recording page says the office accepts cash or check only, with no credit or debit cards. Electronic filers go through approved e-recording partners instead.

faqs.q: What is the Illinois transfer tax rate on a deed?
faqs.a: The state rate is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 stated in the declaration, under 35 ILCS 200/31-10. Mortgage debt the buyer assumes can be excluded from the base when the deed says the transfer is subject to it.

faqs.q: Is a Plat Act affidavit required for every Lee County deed?
faqs.a: Almost every one. The county requires a plat act affidavit or exemption on or with all deeds except those in the Woodhaven Lakes subdivision. The county posts a form on its website.

faqs.q: When are electronic recordings accepted in Lee County?
faqs.a: From 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., and only from approved submitters. The county lists Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile and Hopdox as its current partners.
